holding_summary: Habeas corpus case holding that the city of Yonkers lacked statutory authority to punish, by fine or imprisonment, the Sunday exhibition of moving pictures under its municipal ordinance.
notes: Municipal-power/Sunday-closing case about a moving-picture ordinance; no connection to letting of rooms or dwellings. Selector match ('regulation') is a false positive on unrelated municipal regulation.

holding_summary: Wife with inchoate dower right could not enjoin her husband's grantee from drilling new oil and gas wells, since dower is not an estate and the wells were opened only after the husband's conveyance.
notes: Dower/waste case concerning oil and gas rights; nothing about letting rooms or dwellings for pay. Selector matched generic 'incident of ownership' language unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: Ejectment action by the State to recover 'Gospel and Schools' and 'Literature' lots from squatters; judgment for the State affirmed because defendants failed to connect themselves with any title.
notes: State land-title/ejectment case with no bearing on compensated occupancy of dwellings or rooms. Selector match on 'right to lease' language is a false positive (refers to a town's right to lease a gospel-and-school lot, not residential letting).

holding_summary: A dramatic critic excluded from theatres had no equitable remedy because the Civil Rights Law's penalty provision was his exclusive remedy for exclusion from a place of public accommodation.
notes: Civil Rights Law case about theatre exclusion; the statutory definition of 'place of public accommodation' quoted merely lists inns/hotels for transient guests in passing, but the dispute concerns theatre admission, not lodging arrangements.

holding_summary: A dancing pavilion at a recreation park was not a 'place of public accommodation, resort or amusement' under the Civil Rights Law, so refusing to admit a Black patron did not give rise to statutory liability.
notes: Civil Rights Law case about a dancing pavilion; the same statutory list of inns/hotels for transient guests is quoted in passing but the case does not address lodging or letting of rooms.

holding_summary: A hotel company that cashed a forged check as payee was a holder in due course under the Negotiable Instruments Law and not liable to the drawer or the drawee bank for the proceeds.
notes: Negotiable-instruments/forged-check case; the fact that the drawer resided at an apartment hotel and paid monthly rent is incidental background, not an adjudication of the legal character of the letting arrangement.

holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting use to residential purposes was strictly construed not to cover lots outside the metes-and-bounds description, so an owner could erect a commercial building there.
notes: Restrictive-covenant construction dispute over a commercial building; no discussion of lodging, boarding, or letting of rooms for pay.

holding_summary: A restrictive covenant barring a 'garage' did not prohibit a small lean-to attached to a private dwelling used only to house the owner's own automobile, distinguishing private from public garages.
notes: Restrictive-covenant case about a private garage; the covenant's list of prohibited uses includes 'boarding house' among many other excluded business uses, but the case does not adjudicate anything about lodging or letting.

holding_summary: A railroad's construction of tracks over lots restricted to private residential use violated restrictive covenants benefiting neighboring lot owners, entitling plaintiff to damages measured by lost rental value.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/railroad-easement damages case; the covenant excludes 'flat, tenement or house designed for or occupied by more than two families' among other uses, but no lodging or short-term letting issue is presented.

holding_summary: A title subject to an old restrictive covenant on building setbacks was held unmarketable for specific-performance purposes, regardless of whether changed neighborhood conditions might make the covenant unenforceable in practice.
notes: Stipulated facts note the premises are 'now used for business purposes and as a boarding house' amid a neighborhood that shifted from residential to commercial, but this is background scene-setting for a title-marketability holding, not a ruling on the legal character or regulation of boarding-house use. characterization/polarity left null per hard requirement 1 (no supporting quote on that issue).

holding_summary: In an action by commercial tenants against their landlord for failure to deliver leased basement space, the proper measure of damages was the excess of actual rental value over the rent reserved, and a new trial was ordered.
notes: Commercial loft/basement lease dispute over damages, unrelated to compensated household letting or lodger/boarder arrangements. characterization left null since no quote supports it and it does not bear on the corpus's doctrinal question.

holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting a subdivision to detached one-family dwellings with no flat roof was enforced to enjoin construction of a modern twenty-family apartment house.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/apartment-house case; concerns permanent multi-family construction, not short-term letting of rooms or lodger/boarder status.

holding_summary: A restrictive building-line and garage covenant, part of a subdivision building scheme, was enforced against a defendant who built a garage within the prohibited setback, since a garage is functionally a stable for motor cars.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/setback-and-garage case; no bearing on letting of rooms or dwellings for pay.

holding_summary: A building purchaser who refused to let a former industrial tenant remove fixtures it had been permitted to leave behind was liable for conversion of that property.
notes: Conversion-of-fixtures case involving an ice-manufacturing tenant; no connection to household letting or lodging.

holding_summary: A dress-shop salesman injured while retrieving a garment from the factory floor was not engaged in the 'manufacture' of clothing within the Workmen's Compensation Law, so the award to him was set aside.
notes: Workmen's Compensation Law case about employment classification; wholly unrelated to letting of dwellings or rooms.

holding_summary: A covenant restricting only the first buildings erected to one-family private dwellings did not prevent a later owner from altering the existing building into several apartments, since the covenant restricted construction, not continuing use.
notes: Restrictive-covenant case about converting a single-family dwelling into apartments; concerns permanent multi-family use, not short-term letting of rooms or lodger/boarder arrangements.

holding_summary: A purchaser who intended to erect a business warehouse was excused from specifically performing a land-purchase contract after a zoning resolution enacted between contract and closing restricted the block to residential uses.
notes: The quoted zoning resolution lists 'boarding houses and hotels of a certain size' among permitted uses in a residence district, which is adjacent to the corpus's adverse-regulation theme, but the court does not analyze or rule on that classification -- the holding is about specific performance and unmarketability from a business-use restriction. No supporting quote exists for any characterization/polarity finding, so left null and marked irrelevant per the 'no supporting quote' rule.

holding_summary: Affirmed a robbery conviction; among other rulings, held it was not prejudicial for the prosecutor to comment that defendants had taken rooms at a rooming and boarding house with women they falsely called their wives.
notes: Criminal appeal (robbery); the rooming/boarding house is mentioned only as evidentiary background to the crime and prosecutorial argument, with no holding on the legal character of the lodging arrangement -- a passing mention per the field guidance on procedural cases.
